metadata.title: Trusted foundry & secure microelectronics: US DoD (DMEA/RAMP-C/SHIP), EU Chips Act/IPCEI, UK (NSI Act/Newport), and allied onshoring - wiring a major under-connected node
metadata.frame: Who is allowed to fabricate the chips that go into weapons, crypto roots-of-trust, and critical infrastructure - and how states force that capacity onshore or into 'trusted' hands. Three programs anchor it: the US DoD Trusted Foundry / DMEA accreditation regime (+ RAMP-C leading-edge prototypes, SHIP packaging, the Secure Enclave, run via the S2MARTS OTA), the EU Chips Act + IPCEI microelectronics, and the UK's National Semiconductor Strategy + its NSI-Act national-security divestments (Newport Wafer Fab). This block exists to CONNECT the previously near-isolated 'Trusted_Foundry' node (was degree 1) into the semiconductor, defense-prime, CHIPS-Act, foundry (TSMC/Intel/GF/Samsung), and PQC/quantum threads.
metadata.grade: Program existence, administrators, dated milestones, and the UK divestment actions = FACT (DMEA.osd.mil; Intel/IBM newsrooms; DMEA Trusted Foundry Access III solicitation; EU Chips Act 2.0 EUR-Lex/EC; UK NSI-Act orders; Vishay/Nexperia releases). Dollar ceilings/amounts are as-reported (contract CEILINGS != awards). 'Trusted' assurance actually eliminating supply risk, and whether these programs close the leading-edge gap, are INTERPRETATION/open.
metadata.honest_limits: Accreditation reduces but does not eliminate supply risk (TSMC/Taiwan concentration remains the leading-edge chokepoint; trusted domestic capacity is mostly trailing-edge + low-volume). 'Trusted' is a supply-chain-integrity designation, not a claim that a fab is technically superior. National-security divestment orders (NSI Act) are government ACTIONS; imputing a single motive is avoided - the orders' stated basis is national security; companies (Nexperia) dispute it.
metadata.method: DMEA Trusted IC / TAPO (program since 2003; NSA->DMEA transfer 2015); Intel RAMP-C completion (Intel 18A, S2MARTS/OUSD R&E TAME) + Secure Enclave; IBM DMEA trusted-supplier accreditation (2022-23); Trusted Foundry Access III (DMEA, 2026, ~$576M ceiling); EU Chips Act 2.0 (3 Jun 2026) + IPCEI ME-CT (EUR 21.8B; ~EUR 69B catalysed by Oct-2025); UK National Semiconductor Strategy (GBP 1B/10yr, 2023) + NSI Act 2021 (Newport Wafer Fab divestment 2022 -> Vishay $177M 2024; FTDI Chinese-consortium forced sale by Feb-2027); Rapidus (Japan/METI, 2nm, IBM tech).

edges.notes: The DoD Trusted Foundry mission moved from the NSA to DMEA's Trusted Access Program Office (TAPO) in 2015 (TAPO has run it since 2003) - the same NSA->defense microelectronics lineage that recurs across the surveillance/defense threads (fact).

DMEA/TAPO administers the Trusted Foundry Program: guaranteed US-government access to trusted microelectronics for the typically LOW-VOLUME needs of defense; accredits the whole chain - design, mask, foundry, packaging/assembly, test, broker (fact).
GlobalFoundries (Malta NY; ex-IBM Microelectronics East Fishkill/Essex Jct) is a core DMEA-accredited trusted supplier for defense-grade silicon (fact of accreditation; scope varies).
Intel Foundry is positioned as a leading-edge trusted domestic supplier (RAMP-C + Secure Enclave) - the US bet on onshore <=18A for defense (fact of programs; leading-edge yield/timeline open).

IBM holds DMEA Trusted Supplier accreditation and (Trusted Foundry Access II, 2022-23) establishes secured microelectronics manufacturing FLOWS + embedded security services at commercial advanced fabs (fact).
SkyWater Technology (Bloomington MN) is a US-owned DMEA-accredited/DoD trusted foundry - trailing-edge + specialty (the domestic trusted-but-not-leading-edge tier) (fact).
BAE Systems' Microelectronics Center (Nashua NH) is a long-standing trusted/rad-hard foundry for defense - the prime-owned trusted-fab model (fact).
The program's whole purpose: assured, low-volume, trusted leading-and-legacy parts for weapons systems and NSS - both classified and unclassified (fact).

RAMP-C (Rapid Assured Microelectronics Prototypes - Commercial) was awarded via the S2MARTS Other Transaction Authority, run by the Trusted & Assured Microelectronics office (OUSD R&E) - the OTA money pipe for onshore leading-edge (fact).

Intel Foundry COMPLETED RAMP-C (launched Sep-2021): built IP/EDA/ecosystem on Intel 18A (RibbonFET+PowerVia), taped out + tested defense prototypes, onboarded DIB customers Trusted Semiconductor Solutions + Reliable MicroSystems; declared production-readiness (fact of completion; scale-up open).
RAMP-C exists to give DoD access to domestic LEADING-EDGE (not just trailing-edge trusted) prototypes - directly answering the TSMC/Taiwan leading-edge dependency (fact/intent as stated).
The Secure Enclave program funds a dedicated, walled leading-edge Intel manufacturing capability for DoD (successor focus after RAMP-C) - onshore assured supply of advanced nodes (fact of program).

Dedicated defense access to advanced-node silicon inside a commercial fab - the 'trusted enclave in a commercial environment' model also used by Trusted Foundry Access III (~$576M ceiling, DMEA 2026) (fact; ceiling != awards).
edges.source: #232 trusted foundry (Trusted Foundry Access III solicitation)

edges.notes: SHIP (State-of-the-art Heterogeneous Integrated Packaging) gives DoD access to advanced 2.5D/3D packaging + chiplets - packaging is the other half of trusted assurance, not just the fab (fact).
DARPA's microelectronics work (Electronics Resurgence Initiative; SHIELD/AMS provenance) feeds trust/assurance techniques into the trusted-foundry regime - the research arm of hardware trust (fact).
Defense primes depend on DMEA-accredited trusted parts for weapons programs - the demand side that justifies the trusted-foundry regime (fact of dependency).
RTX/Raytheon (like other primes) sources trusted/rad-hard microelectronics for missiles/radar/EW - same trusted-supply dependency (fact).

PQC/crypto roots-of-trust (key storage, secure boot, HSMs) must be fabricated in trusted facilities - hardware assurance underpins the PQC migration; ties this block to the quantum/PQC + ECDSA threads (fact/interpretation).

The reason the regime exists: leading-edge fabrication is concentrated at TSMC (Taiwan), a single-point geopolitical chokepoint; trusted-foundry + CHIPS onshoring are the hedge (interpretation grounded in the Taiwan-silicon-shield thread).
CHIPS & Science Act: Intel is the largest US CHIPS awardee (AZ/OH/NM/OR); pairs with Secure Enclave to onshore leading-edge for both commercial + defense (fact; disbursement/milestones vary).
CHIPS award to GF (Malta NY + Essex Jct VT) - explicitly incl. essential/defense chips (auto, aerospace, defense) at trailing/specialty nodes (fact).
CHIPS-backed TSMC Arizona (leading-edge on US soil) - the onshoring of the very chokepoint the trusted regime worries about (fact).
CHIPS-backed Samsung Taylor TX fab - second leading-edge foreign foundry onshored under US industrial policy (fact).

EU Chips Act + IPCEI ME/CT (EUR 21.8B; EUR 13.7B state aid) span the value chain; ~EUR 69B catalysed by Oct-2025; a third IPCEI + Chips Act 2.0 (adopted 3-Jun-2026) shift toward supply-chain-resilience + a B2B supply platform (fact).
edges.source: #232 trusted foundry (EU Chips Act 2.0 EUR-Lex; SEMI Europe)

edges.notes: Europe's crown-jewel chokepoint is equipment: ASML (EUV monopoly). Draghi urged a fast-track IPCEI for lithography/deposition leadership - the EU's leverage point in the allied stack (fact/interpretation).
edges.source: #232 trusted foundry (Draghi report; EU Chips Act 2.0)

edges.notes: ESMC Dresden (TSMC JV with Bosch/Infineon/NXP) - EU onshoring of a leading foundry, mirroring the US CHIPS play (fact).
edges.source: #232 trusted foundry (EU Chips Act; ESMC Dresden)

edges.notes: IPCEI funds the FULL chain incl. materials/equipment - wiring the trusted/industrial-policy layer to the existing semiconductor materials + equipment nodes (fact).

Reports that the EU + member states are preparing to join the US-led 'Pax Silica' initiative on AI-chip supply chains - resilience via trusted international partnership, not pure autarky (fact of reports; graded).
US-led allied framework to align AI-chip supply chains among trusted partners - the geopolitical layer above national trusted-foundry programs (fact of initiative; details emerging).

UK National Semiconductor Strategy (GBP 1B/10yr, up to GBP 200M 2023-25) - deliberately NICHE (design, compound semiconductors, R&D; not leading-edge fabrication); Newport is the UK's largest fab (200mm, >30k wafers/mo, automotive) (fact; scale small vs US/EU).

Under the National Security and Investment Act 2021 the UK ordered divestment of 86% of Newport Wafer Fab (Nov-2022) after two prior clearances - the marquee NSI intervention (fact; national-security basis stated; Nexperia disputes).
edges.source: #232 trusted foundry (UK NSI Act order 2022; MoFo)

edges.notes: Nexperia (Dutch-incorporated, ultimately China-owned via Wingtech) had bought 100% by Jul-2021; ordered to divest 86%; said it was 'shocked' and denied the national-security concerns (present both accounts) (fact).
Sold to US-based Vishay Intertechnology for ~$177M (completed Mar-2024, after UK approval) - forced Chinese exit -> allied ownership (fact).
The pattern extends: UK ordered a Chinese consortium to sell 80.2% of chipmaker FTDI by Feb-2027 (legal challenges failed) - mirroring Newport; retroactive review of PRC-linked chip stakes (fact).
Rapidus (METI-backed, Hokkaido) targets 2nm using IBM technology - Japan's onshoring + allied leading-edge bet, part of the same trusted/allied-supply pattern (fact; yield/timeline unproven).
Rapidus licenses IBM's 2nm nanosheet technology - the IBM-microelectronics lineage (also behind GF and DMEA trusted services) reaching into allied Japan (fact).
